verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Repair the KP14 truth (regenerate integ_results.npz + G_func.csv, fix H/L regime convention)
verdicts.critique: I verified the central claim directly and it is worse than described. utils_kp14/KP14_solfiles/integ_results.npz reports 762/1000 'nonzero' entries, but that count is meaningless: reading G_up_lst on the eps grid from G_func.csv over the interval the panel actually occupies (eps in [0.93,1.066], grid indices 185-212) gives 0.0, 1.25e-111, 2.25e-72, 1.39e-41, 6.01e-19, and only at index 212 does it jump to 1.718e3 -- against the underlying G_up values of 1523, 1559, 1597, 1637, 1678, 1721 on the same nodes. So E_t[G] is between 40 and 120 orders of magnitude too small everywhere the simulation lives, and term2 in panel_functions_kp14.py:193 (Et_z_alph*Et_x*Et_G) is identically zero. erets at line 199 is therefore (term1+term3+term4)/price - 1, i.e. minus the PVGO share, which is exactly the reported rp = -PVGO/P artifact. Everything downstream -- rp, cond_var, max_sr, sdf_ret, the correlations.csv 'true' column, the -2.64/-5.35 FF/FM Sharpes -- is a quadrature failure, not economics. Two corrections to the proposal. (i) The regime fix (c)/(d): I confirmed panel_functions_kp14.py:98 gives stationary P(high)=mu_L/(mu_H+mu_L)=0.6809 while config.py:257 normalizes LAMBDA_L assuming w=MU_H/(MU_H+MU_L)=0.3191, and that the alternative repair (renormalize LAMBDA_L at w=0.6809) yields LAMBDA_L=-1.88, impossible. But the proposer did not consider the third option: keep the sim and cap LAMBDA_H at 1.47 (the largest value consistent with LAMBDA_L>=0 under P(high)=0.6809). Flipping the sim instead preserves the 2.35/0.367 H-L spread, which is the right call for cross-sectional dispersion, but it should be stated as a choice, not a forced move. (ii) The predicted max_sr of 0.223/month is the SDF's own bound sqrt(gamma_x^2+gamma_z^2)/sqrt(12), not the attainable stock-cross-section Sharpe. Since beta_x = 1 for every firm (price is homogeneous of degree 1 in x at panel_functions_kp14.py:165,173; sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 factors Et_x2[t] out of the whole cross-firm block) and beta_z = alph*share has tiny dispersion, the attainable number will be ~gamma_x/sqrt(12) = 0.199/month with a sliver from z. Expect all three methods to cluster at 0.19-0.20 against a 0.20 ceiling.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It will not, and the proposer says so. Worse than neutral for the paper's thesis: after the repair the truth becomes rp_i = gamma_x*sigma_x*dt + alph*gamma_z*sigma_z*dt*share_i, an EXACT affine function of a single scalar (share), and the proposer's own check shows VAP_i/book_i has cross-sectional sd of only 3.2% of its mean, so share_i = 1 - v_i*bm_i with v_i near-constant and FM's raw-bm column spans the entire z-channel to within a few percent. FM's span in fama_functions.py:158-160 is literally the column space of [1, raw chars]; bm is one of those columns. FF's hml 2x3 sort (fama_functions.py:84-104) is a tercile step approximation to the same monotone object, so FF will be a few points behind FM and DKKM will be within noise of FM. The repaired table will show a CLEANER null than today's, because today's -2.64/-5.35 at least look like a difference. The one genuinely favorable side effect: with SR* falling from 10.0/month to ~0.20/month, HJD stops being pinned at its 0.269 floor and acquires real dynamic range (at SR*=0.2 the span between rho=0 and rho=1 is wide), so the metric becomes able to discriminate -- it just will not have anything to discriminate.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt as a hard prerequisite. Two additions the proposer omits. (1) Propagate max_sr from moments into results.pkl -- utils/evaluate_sdfs.py never carries it through, so no table can currently report Sharpe/SR*, which is the only interpretable number and the single cheapest diagnostic for every other proposal. (2) Add a regression test that asserts E_t[G_up](eps) is within a few percent of G_up(eps) at eps=1.0 (the CIR transition sd at sigma_eps=0.02, dt=1/12 is ~0.006, so E_t[G] must be close to G itself); the current file fails that assertion by 50 orders of magnitude and would have been caught instantly.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: K priced technology-domain IST shocks over an observable 2-D technology map
verdicts.critique: The algebra checks out: I verified alph*(3*alpha-1)/(1-alpha) == 2*alph^2 - alph identically, so E_t[z_i'^a z_j'^a] = Et_z_alph_i * Et_z_alph_j * exp(a^2 rho_ij sigma_z^2 dt) reduces exactly to the existing Et_z_alph2 at rho_ij=1, and the sdf_compute change really is a precomputed elementwise multiply on an N x N matrix. This is the only proposal in the set that satisfies condition C3 (many quasi-orthogonal priced directions). But three of its supporting claims are wrong. (1) THE BANDWIDTH PRESCRIPTION IS BACKWARDS. I built the exact rff() code path (rank_standardize chars, W = gamma*N(0,1), [sin;cos], rank_standardize again) on the proposal's own construction (K=100, h=0.10, L=7 rank chars, 360 features, N=1000) and measured cross-sectional R^2 on g(theta) = p(theta).gamma. Coded GAMMA_GRID: 0.730. Rescaled by 4.31 as the proposal demands: 0.720. Rescaled by 22 (what you would actually need to resolve an h=0.10 bump on a unit torus, ~31 rad/unit): 0.373. Widening HURTS, exactly as the GS21 agent found. The proposal's headline 2.19x is derived from a generic 'effective rank rises 16.5 -> 78' argument that says nothing about resolution in the two theta directions specifically -- and an isotropic direction in R^7 puts only sqrt(2/7) of its length in the theta plane. (2) HALF THE MEASURED R^2 IS DIMENSION COUNTING. Placebo: 360 pure-noise columns on 1000 firms attain R^2 = 0.343 on g, and RFF360 built on 5 chars carrying NO theta information attains 0.351. So RFF360's 0.730 is ~0.58 of real signal, against quad7 (35 terms, placebo ~0.035) at 0.458 and linear-7 at 0.242. Honest unspanned-variance shares are FM 0.24 / explicit-quadratic 0.44 / DKKM 0.58, not 0.03 / -- / 0.45. Recomputing the proposal's own Sharpe budget (SR*^2 = 0.476 + 0.244 + 9.00) gives FM 1.70/yr, DKKM 2.44/yr, ratio 1.43x -- not 2.19x, and not the 3-5x target. (3) THE BENCHMARK IS HANDICAPPED BY CONSTRUCTION. The proposal gives FM and FF two continuous scalars theta1, theta2. But the empirical analogue it cites (patent classes, TNIC, industry) is CATEGORICAL with ~100 levels, and the standard practice is dummies. A cross-sectional regression with 100 domain dummies on 1000 firms -- which is what fama_macbeth's X @ pinvh(X'X) at fama_functions.py:158-160 would produce if you handed it the dummies -- spans ALL K modes EXACTLY, and FM beats DKKM. The DKKM advantage here is entirely an artifact of choosing an encoding the benchmark cannot use.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures it if you encode theta the way a real researcher would (domain dummies), which is the natural encoding of the exact empirical objects the proposal cites -- and then FM is not approximating g at all, it is spanning it, and DKKM loses. Even with the continuous-coordinate encoding, an explicit quadratic in 7 chars gets 0.44 of 0.58, so DKKM's marginal contribution over 'FM plus interaction terms' is 32%, i.e. sqrt of that in Sharpe on the unspanned budget only. And the estimation side is hostile: 360 features against T=360 is exactly c=1, the double-descent point where the existing BOP results already show BGN Sharpe collapsing to 0.006 and HJD to 18.5 at alpha=0. Finally the theta coordinates and the gamma_k vector are drawn ONCE and are time-invariant, so g(theta_i) is a static cross-sectional variable -- 360 months of data to learn one fixed smooth 3-D function of (share, theta1, theta2), which is a much easier problem than the real-data one and is exactly the regime where a modestly-flexible small model wins.
verdicts.salvage: The idea survives, but reframe it. (a) Drop the GAMMA_GRID rescale entirely -- I measured that it hurts. (b) Make the technology field UNOBSERVABLE and inferable only through its footprint in the other characteristics (e.g. domain affects the arrival-rate regime, the capital intensity, and the cash-flow seasonality) rather than handing everyone theta1, theta2. That kills the dummy-variable objection and it is more faithful to the real-data situation, where technology exposure is not a column in Compustat. (c) Report the placebo (K random Gaussian directions carrying no economics) in every span table, or the 360-feature number cannot be interpreted. (d) Report the DKKM/FM ratio at N=250, 500, 1000 -- if it moves with N you have measured diversification. (e) Keep alpha=0.75 for transversality; that arithmetic I could not fault.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Historical-cost book value plus vintage/count/investment-intensity/cash-flow-volatility characteristics
verdicts.critique: The mechanism claim is that beta_z,i = alph*(1 - bm_i*exp(c0 + c1*age_i)) is a product of two non-size characteristics that FM cannot form. That is true as a statement about function spaces and false as a statement about Sharpe. Under exact K-factor pricing -- which is what KP14 is after P1, with mu = B*lambda and Sigma = B*S_f*B' + D -- the attainable Sharpe of ANY portfolio w is SR(w)^2 = lambda'... = 1/(sigma_f^2 + w'Dw/(w'beta)^2) in the 1-factor case, and the shortfall of a mis-specified beta is governed by the idiosyncratic term, which is O(1/N). I ran the exact experiment with the proposal's own structures: beta_x bilinear (P5), beta_z = 3*share with share = 1 - bm*exp(-0.2 + 0.03*age) (P3's bm x age), dispersed char-linked idio variance sd(log d) = 0.66 (P4), and a linear span containing only {1, log(1/sd), bm, age, kappa, sales/price, share} with NO products. Result: the best linear-span portfolio attains 96.6% / 99.1% / 99.7% of SR* at N = 250 / 1000 / 4000, and adding all 21 quadratic terms takes it to 99.7% / 99.9% / 100.0%. At the production N=1000 the ENTIRE nonlinearity headroom created by bm x age plus bilinear beta_x plus 20x idio-variance dispersion is 0.9 percentage points of Sharpe, and it vanishes as 1/N. That is the whole proposal.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures it to 99.1% at N=1000 by the measurement above, with no interaction terms at all, because the object is a LOADING and loadings only need to be right up to a diversification residual. FF also gets a free pass here that the proposal ignores: prepare_panel sets size = log(mve) (utils_factors/factor_utils.py, ROOT line 62), and every FF weight in fama_functions.py:70-113 is proportional to mve_i = exp(size_i). FF therefore carries an exponential-in-a-characteristic that neither FM (linear in log mve) nor DKKM (features capped in [-0.5,0.5] by the second rank_standardize at dkkm_functions.py:110) can form. If the target tilt has any size-level component -- and under P4's d ~ 1/nlive ~ 1/mve it is exactly proportional to mve -- FF's mkt_rf column IS the answer. Finally, the historical-cost change makes bm a NOISIER proxy for share; the KP14 diagnosis already measured eps at only 5.6% linearly / 15.0% quadratically recoverable from chars, so the added noise is unlearnable for every estimator and dilutes DKKM's residual edge along with everyone else's.
verdicts.salvage: Two pieces survive, neither for the stated reason. (1) The char additions are the cheapest available route to raising L, which is the one lever that reliably raises RFF effective rank (the theory agent measured 16.5 at L=5, 38.5 at L=10, 98.3 at L=20, 432 at L=50). But go far beyond four columns -- see missed ideas. (2) Before adopting historical-cost book, run the diagnostic the proposal itself specifies (R^2 of true share on linear chars vs. all pairwise products) and abandon the change if the quadratic gain is under 0.10; the KP14 diagnosis already measured 0.717 linear-raw vs 0.677 rank+quadratic, i.e. the gain is NEGATIVE in the space DKKM actually operates in. Drop the bm x age Sharpe claim entirely.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Recalibrate theta_eps/sigma_eps and project count so idiosyncratic variance stops being 1/size
verdicts.critique: The economics is right and the current calibration is indefensible: theta_eps = 0.35 (config.py:247) implies a firm-TFP half-life of 2 years and sigma_eps = 0.1*0.2 = 0.02 gives a stationary sd of 0.024, against Syverson's within-industry sd(log TFP) of 0.3-0.6 and annual persistence of 0.90-0.95. Fixing it is correct on its own terms and it removes the mechanism behind KP14's negative Sharpes. But as a source of DKKM advantage it is dead twice over. First, the D^-1 channel under exact factor pricing is O(1/N): my span experiment above gave FM 99.1% of SR* at N=1000 with sd(log d) = 0.66 already in place. Second -- and this is the part the proposal misses -- the change is actively ANTI-DKKM given the estimator as coded. dkkm_functions.rff line 110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a second time, so every DKKM regressor is a bounded uniform on [-0.4995, 0.4995] and no feature can be large-amplitude on a small subset of firms. The object DKKM needs is 1/d_i, which is exp(-b'x) -- monotone, heavy-tailed, and amplitude-carrying. rank_standardize is invariant to monotone transformations, so rank_standardize(sin(gamma*w'x)) = rank_standardize(w'x) for the ~76% of directions where sin is monotone over the cross-section; DKKM sees the ORDERING of 1/d and never its SCALE. FM, by contrast, regresses on RAW unstandardized characteristics (fama_functions.py:152-160, the standardization block is commented out), so it retains raw scale. The KP14 diagnosis measured exactly this: [1, 5 raw chars] attains 70.1% of SR* while [1, 5 rank chars] attains only 64.2% and [1, ranks, 15 quadratic rank interactions] 68.6% -- the rank-space nonlinear basis loses to the raw linear basis.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FF captures it better than DKKM does. If d_i is char-linked and the tilt is inverse-variance, the optimal weight is w* proportional to beta_i/d_i, and under the current 1/nlive mechanism that is proportional to mve_i -- which is precisely FF's value weighting. Even after this proposal weakens the link (the proposal's own arithmetic takes the non-diversifying share only from 2.2% to 24%, leaving corr(log d, log nlive) around -0.85 versus a real-data target of -0.35), the residual is still dominantly size. And the magnitude is second-order regardless: even at 20x dispersion in d the theory agent measured SR(equal-weight)/SR* = 0.998 at N=1000. In basis points, this proposal is worth roughly 20 bp of monthly Sharpe out of ~200 bp available, i.e. 1%, and it hands most of that to FF.
verdicts.salvage: Adopt the theta_eps/sigma_eps recalibration on CORRECTNESS grounds only -- it is needed to stop 97.8% of firm risk being 'did a plant close', and it is needed to break the size artifact documented in docs/kp14_size_idio_var.md. Drop the DKKM-advantage claim. The one variant worth pursuing is the extension buried at the end: heterogeneous sigma_eps,i drawn INDEPENDENTLY of lambda_f and hence of size, reported as cfvol. That makes d orthogonal to size, which is the actual fix for the negative-Sharpe artifact. But it will only pay in Sharpe if paired with a genuine unspanned premium (P2 or P6), and it will only pay for DKKM if the second rank_standardize at dkkm_functions.py:110 is replaced by an amplitude-preserving standardization -- an estimator change nobody in this set proposes.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Heterogeneous operating leverage (firm-specific fixed cost per project)
verdicts.critique: This is the clearest case of confusing loading dispersion with Sharpe. Yes, beta_x is currently exactly 1 for every firm -- I confirmed the mechanism: price = VAP + PVGO with VAP = x*sum K^alpha*A (panel_functions_kp14.py:165) and PVGO = z^alph * x * lambda_f * G(eps) (line 173), x factors out of both, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 hard-codes the consequence by multiplying the entire cross-firm block by the scalar Et_x2[t]. And yes, adding a fixed cost makes beta_x,i = 1 + kappa_i*(Rev_i/P_i)/(r+delta), a genuine product of two non-size characteristics that FM's [1, chars] span cannot form and FF's size-crossed tercile sorts cannot form. But x is a SINGLE priced factor. With mu = beta*lambda_x and Sigma = beta*beta'*sigma_f^2 + D, the maximum attainable Sharpe is lambda_x/sigma_f * sqrt(beta'D^-1 beta*sigma_f^2/(1+beta'D^-1 beta*sigma_f^2)), which converges to gamma_x as N grows regardless of how dispersed beta is. Numerically with beta ~ 1, d ~ (5%/mo)^2, N = 1000: beta'D^-1 beta = 400,000, so the idiosyncratic correction is 2.5e-6 against sigma_f^2 = 1.4e-3, i.e. 0.18%. A portfolio using a linear approximation beta_hat with cosine 0.9 to the true beta raises that to 3.1e-6, and the Sharpe ratio between the two is sqrt(1 - 4e-4) = 0.9998. FOUR BASIS POINTS of relative Sharpe. The proposal's predicted 1.15-1.30x standalone is off by roughly three orders of magnitude, and it is the only proposal in the set that predicts a large gap at the CODED bandwidth, so this error is load-bearing for the whole set.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Both FF and FM capture it to within a fraction of a basis point, for the same reason: cross-sectional dispersion in the loading on a single priced factor is worth only the diversification residual, which is O(1/N). My span experiment with bilinear beta_x explicitly included and NO product terms in the span gave FM-linear = 99.1% of SR* at N=1000 and 99.7% at N=4000. The equal-weighted market already has beta_x ~ 1.2 and captures gamma_x. Separately, the proposal is the most expensive in the set: it breaks the x-homogeneity that sdf_compute_kp14.py:167 exploits, requiring new closed forms for E[n'Q'] and E[n'^2] on the diagonal and a full re-derivation of the term4 double-counting correction at lines 162-165. That is the highest-risk surgery in the set purchased for four basis points. There is also a live blow-up risk the proposal only half-flags: for a high-kappa firm in a bad eps state, P_i = VAP - n_i*f_i/(r+delta) can go to zero or negative, and sdf_compute_kp14.py:269 filters only on book > 0, not price > 0. A near-zero price makes 1+eret and the whole ER row explode, and scipy.linalg.solve with assume_a='pos' returns garbage without raising -- the exact 1e57 max_sr pathology already documented in the comment block at lines 262-268.
verdicts.salvage: Almost nothing. The only defensible residue: if you want beta_x dispersion for its own sake (so that the CAPM row in the table stops being degenerate and the 25-portfolio GRS test has any factor structure to reject), a fixed cost is the right way to get it, and it costs nothing in the Sharpe metric either way. Do NOT present it as a source of DKKM advantage. If it is adopted, add price > 0 to the keep mask at sdf_compute_kp14.py:269 and assert min(price) is bounded away from zero.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: Persistent mean-reverting demand wedge on price
verdicts.critique: This is the only proposal that satisfies condition C2 -- an expected-return component that is NOT minus a covariance and whose contribution alpha'D^-1 alpha grows with N. The parameter derivation is sound (I reproduced sd(alpha) = (1-e^{-0.135/12})*0.15 = 0.00168/month, and the implied 2.25%/month extra idiosyncratic vol is a move toward real-data levels). The lognormal OU moments really are elementary and really do keep sdf_compute at O(N^2) via outer(a,a). But the LEARNABILITY argument, which is the whole mechanism, does not survive contact with the KP14 diagnosis. The proposal's own identity is w_i = -log bm_i - h(chars_i) with h = log(P^fund/book). In KP14, P^fund/book = (VAP + PVGO)/book and the proposal itself measured VAP/book = (1/alpha)*[a factor with cross-sectional sd of 3.2%], so h = const - log(1 - share_i) up to a 3% wobble. That is a UNIVARIATE MONOTONE CONVEX transform of a single scalar, not a rich multi-characteristic map. DKKM's incremental recovery of alpha over FM is bounded by the incremental R^2 of a nonlinear-vs-linear fit of share -- and the KP14 diagnosis already measured that increment: share R^2 = 0.717 on 5 raw chars linear, 0.464 on 5 rank chars linear, 0.677 on rank chars plus all quadratic interactions. The nonlinear rank-space basis is WORSE than the raw linear basis. So the expected DKKM-minus-FM recovery of alpha is approximately zero or negative, and the residual (share is driven by eps, which is 5.6% linearly / 15.0% quadratically recoverable) is unlearnable noise for everyone. A second, quieter problem: the wedge contaminates log bm directly, so log bm alone -- which FM sees via raw bm and DKKM sees via rank(bm), the same ordering -- already correlates strongly with w. If sd(log(V/B)) ~ 0.2 and sd(w) = 0.15, the wedge is ~36% of the variance of log bm, so bm ALONE is a 0.6-correlation signal for alpha, available to FM at zero cost.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures most of it because the wedge is revealed by a single raw characteristic (bm) net of a monotone univariate correction. DKKM's advantage is confined to the curvature of -log(1-share), which is one-dimensional and which rank-standardization partly reproduces for free. Quantifying the proposal's own accounting honestly: if FM recovers 55% of var(alpha) and DKKM 65% (rather than the assumed 40%/70%-90%), SR_DKKM/SR_FM = sqrt((0.65*1.79+0.05)/(0.55*1.79+0.05)) = 1.08x, not 1.33-2.4x. Three further attacks. (a) The near-arbitrage is a pure sqrt(N) artifact -- the proposal flags this but understates it: with alpha independent across firms, SR*^2 = N*E[alpha^2/d] scales linearly in N, so the headline Sharpe of 1.36/month is entirely a statement about N=1000 and would be 0.68 at N=250. (b) The Sharpe metric as coded is scale-invariant month by month (evaluate_sdfs.py:183-199, create_slides_tables.py:34-42 form mean/stdev per month then average), so it gives ZERO credit for the timing channel -- and a mean-reverting wedge is precisely a timing story. (c) The term4 unbundling at sdf_compute_kp14.py:162-165 is a genuine correctness hazard: the existing -outer(cf/P, cf/P) correction is valid only because the two legs share a normalization, and the two commented-out single-pair tests at lines 148-159 and 231-254 must be reactivated before any number is trusted.
verdicts.salvage: The proposal is right about WHAT is missing (an unspanned, N-scaling premium) and wrong about WHAT MAKES IT HARD TO FIND. Two changes make it work. (1) Give the wedge a FACTOR STRUCTURE with characteristic-dependent loadings -- a small number of crowded-trade / flow factors whose exposures are nonlinear functions of several characteristics -- rather than i.i.d. firm-level noise. That satisfies C2 and C3 simultaneously and is at least as defensible empirically (Koijen-Yogo demand system, index and flow effects) as pure noise-trader OU. (2) Make the wedge's AMPLITUDE characteristic-dependent, sigma_w,i = f(chars), so the optimal weight alpha_i/d_i is a genuine ratio with BOTH numerator and denominator char-linked -- that is the configuration in which the theory agent measured the RFF-over-linear ceiling ratio hit 6-21x, versus 1.0 for a linear alpha. Also run the proposal's own pre-flight diagnostic (R^2 of true w on linear chars vs. degree-3) and abort if the linear R^2 exceeds 0.85; on the numbers already in hand it will.

missed_ideas: THE WITHIN-FIRM PROJECT DISTRIBUTION IS A FREE SOURCE OF 30-50 CHARACTERISTICS, AND NOBODY USES IT. KP14 already simulates K[t1,t2,n], chi, uj and Kj per project (panel_functions_kp14.py:126-152). Every firm-month therefore carries a full distribution over 6-24 live projects. Moments of that distribution -- HHI of capital across projects, sd and skewness of project vintages, fraction of capital in the largest project, dispersion of project-level u, age of the oldest and newest project, count of projects created in the last 12/36/60 months, capital-weighted vs equal-weighted mean age -- are dozens of genuinely distinct, weakly-informative, mutually non-redundant characteristics that require ZERO model change and ZERO re-solve. The theory agent measured RFF effective rank going 16.5 (L=5) -> 38.5 (L=10) -> 98.3 (L=20) -> 432 (L=50). Raising L from 5 to ~35 is the single cheapest way to move the estimator from DKKM's APT regime (EffRank ~2.5, complexity harmful) toward their AIPT regime (EffRank ~500), and it is far more defensible than inventing an observable technology coordinate. P3 gestures at this with four columns and stops.

PRICE THE PROJECT-ARRIVAL SHOCK. 97.8% of KP14's idiosyncratic variance is currently Poisson project death and arrival, and every bit of it is UNPRICED. Making a component of the arrival intensity aggregate (a technology-diffusion wave common across firms, with firm-specific exposure through lambda_f and the H/L regime) and giving it a price of risk turns the model's dominant source of return variance into a priced factor whose loading is multiplicative in intensity -- genuinely nonlinear, and orthogonal to both the x and z channels. This is a smaller change than P2's technology map and it repurposes machinery that already exists (sim_arrivals at panel_functions_kp14.py:91-107).

THE DOUBLE RANK-STANDARDIZATION IS A MODEL-INDEPENDENT CEILING AND NO PROPOSAL TOUCHES IT. dkkm_functions.py:110 rank-standardizes the sin/cos features a second time. Because rank-standardization is invariant to monotone transformations, this makes GAMMA_GRID a near-no-op for the ~76% of directions where sin is monotone over the cross-section, and it forces every one of the 3600 regressors to the identical bounded uniform marginal. No feature can be large-amplitude on a small subset of firms. Any proposal whose target weight is amplitude-carrying -- 1/d (P4), exp(size), a heavy-tailed alpha -- is structurally unreachable no matter what the model does. P2's gamma rescale does not fix this and I measured that it makes span WORSE. The minimal fix (winsorize then standardize to unit variance, preserving the sin/cos amplitude equalization that rank-standardization was accidentally supplying) is orthogonal to all six proposals and is plausibly worth more than any of them.

NMAT=5 WEIGHT AVERAGING SUPPRESSES THE MECHANISM BEING TESTED. estimate_sdf_dkkm.py averages stock weights across 5 independent W draws. Averaging M random-feature ridge fits of the SAME target on the SAME months converges to kernel ridge with the same explicit penalty, cancelling exactly the draw-specific high-frequency directions and mechanically flattening the Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve -- which is the curve the paper is trying to measure. config.py notes the root codebase used nmat=1. Setting NMAT=1 and reporting the 5 draws as replications is free and should be done before any economic change is evaluated.

agr IS A DEGENERATE CHARACTERISTIC IN KP14 AND IT ASYMMETRICALLY PENALIZES DKKM. Investment in KP14 is a Poisson event, so book jumps discretely and agr is mostly exactly zero (the same pathology the BGN agent quantified at 87-92% ties). rank_standardize breaks those ties with np.argsort (dkkm_functions.py:57-62), producing a persistent pseudo-random column that enters all 3600 RFF features MULTIPLICATIVELY while polluting only one of FM's six additive regressors, and it degenerates FF's cma tercile sort to q30 == q70. Measure the tie fraction in the KP14 panel and either drop agr or replace it with a smoothed multi-year investment rate before attributing any DKKM shortfall to economics.

NO PROPOSAL CREATES A CHARACTERISTIC x MACRO-STATE INTERACTION, WHICH IS THE ONLY CONDITIONING CHANNEL THE ESTIMATOR CAN SEE. The DKKM ridge coefficient is a single vector estimated over 360 months and applied unchanged to every cross-section, and KP14's feature map has no time-varying input at all (dkkm_functions.rff appends rf only for model == 'bgn', line 95). Time-varying prices of risk are one of the two channels through which complexity pays in the DKKM/KMZ theory, and in KP14 they are invisible by construction. Any conditioning story must be built so that the premium of a characteristic moves with a state that is itself readable from the cross-section (e.g. cross-sectional dispersion of PVGO share as a proxy for the IST cycle).

MEASUREMENT ERROR AND REPORTING LAGS ARE THE CHEAPEST DEFENSIBLE WAY TO MAKE THE SMALL MODEL MIS-SPECIFIED. Every characteristic in these panels is observed exactly, with no missing values, no accounting lag, and no reporting discretion, and N is fixed at 1000 with no entry or exit. In that environment the 6-regressor model is correctly specified and ridge over 3600 features can only add variance. Reporting each characteristic as a noisy, lagged, partially-missing proxy -- and supplying several redundant-but-imperfect proxies for the same latent state, which is what real characteristic datasets look like -- is a minimal change that makes shrinkage-over-a-rich-basis the statistically right answer. This is the mechanism that lets DKKM's five-characteristic real-data model reach 1.93-2.50 while these models' five characteristics reach nothing.

A FAT-TAILED SIZE DISTRIBUTION WITH ENTRY AND EXIT. DKKM's real-data Sharpe falls from 3.7 to ~1.6 when restricted to mega/large caps, so a large share of the empirical virtue of complexity is a microcap phenomenon: small, high-idiosyncratic-volatility, high-alpha names. KP14 already produces zero-project firms (~5% per month, currently a nuisance masked out at sdf_compute_kp14.py:269). Turning that into genuine entry and exit with a Pareto size distribution and a size-dependent alpha and idio vol would reproduce the tail where the real gap lives.

THE TEST ASSETS HAVE NO POWER AND NO PROPOSAL FIXES THEM. utils/generate_25_portfolios.py sorts only on mve and bm -- two of the five characteristics every method already spans linearly -- and compute_pricing_errors.py runs each method's MVE return as a single factor against them. Any proposal that creates nonlinear or interactive mispricing will be invisible to the GRS test. Add portfolios sorted on deciles of the model's OWN true conditional SDF weight, and on characteristic interactions.

REPORT SHARPE/SR* AND THE SPAN-CEILING DIAGNOSTIC BEFORE RUNNING ANY ESTIMATOR. max_sr is computed in every sdf_loop and stored in the moments pickles but never propagated by utils/evaluate_sdfs.py into results.pkl. Every one of these six proposals can be pre-screened in minutes without touching the estimator: per month compute sqrt(mu' X (X' Sigma X)^-1 X' mu) for X = [1, chars] and for X = the configured RFF, take the ratio, and report it alongside a PLACEBO basis of the same width carrying no characteristic information. My placebo here (360 pure-noise columns attaining R^2 = 0.343 on 1000 firms) shows that roughly half of any 360-feature span number is dimension counting; without that control the span tables are uninterpretable.
